sentences: Key findings: Fully four-fifths (80%) of the countries holding elections in 2024 had GenAI incidents.

It is based on the IPIE’s capturing all reported political uses of GenAI across all 50 countries holding competitive elections in 2024, from deepfakes to precision voter targeting, including coordinated campaigns and foreign interference.
The IPIE’s recent assessment shows that 80% of the countries that held elections in 2024 had GenAI incidents.
The IPIE’s new Technical Paper, The Role of Generative AI Use in 2024 Elections Worldwide: Searching for Solutions , is based on the first open-access database of GenAI election incidents.
The incident database records which actors used GenAI and how, and evaluates the role of GenAI in campaign communications, public opinion formation, and election turnout.
The IPIE’s assessment shows that more than two-thirds of reported GenAI incidents (69%) were portrayed as having a harmful role in the election.
More than two-thirds (69%) of the incidents were cataloged as having a harmful role in the election.

The IPIE’s work on this topic fills the current gap in global insights on the impact of GenAI in political content proliferation and provides data-driven analysis to inform policy recommendations that strengthen election administration in democracies.
There is a wide range of expert views on the use of GenAI in political contexts, including its potential to impact voters’ behavior on a scale and interfere with election integrity.
It remains difficult to measure the specific impact of GenAI—or any technology—on particular elections.
But the use of GenAI for electioneering is no longer speculative or theoretical, it is observable and global.

Built from rigorous analysis of global media and vetted by a scientific panel, the findings offer the most authoritative account to date of how synthetic content is reshaping the practice of elections.
The vast majority (90%) of incidents involved content creation, such as audio messages, images, videos, and social media posts.

Almost half of the incidents have no known source (46%), a quarter were produced by political candidates and parties (25%), a fifth were produced by foreign actors (20%), and the remainder came from other sources (9%).
In 2024, the potential benefits of these technologies were largely eclipsed by their harmful misuse.
This demonstrates the widespread use and availability of GenAI technology as well as the political will to rely on it across the world.
Professor Sebastian Valenzuela , Chief Science Officer of the IPIE, said: This technical paper makes it clear: GenAI is no longer a future threat, it’s a present force.
